title: Sunday · the empty town, ii
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · from 2017 the aggregator
logline: Main street on a Sunday in March with nobody. The lockboxes unturned. Gully's OPEN sign lit for no one. The strip doesn't say why.

panels.composition: Tier 1: main street at noon, no cars, no people, the lockboxes on the doors with their dials untouched, a gull walking down the center line.
props: a gull on the center line

image.prompt: wet-on-wet watercolor in gray-green moss, fog and rusted tin, a small-town main street at noon completely empty of cars and people with lockboxes on every door and a single gull walking down the center line, no words

panels.name: Street

panels.composition: Tier 2: Gully's OPEN sign lit in the window, the counter behind it, the end stool, nobody on the customer side.

image.prompt: wet-on-wet watercolor in gray-green moss, fog and rusted tin, a lit OPEN sign in a shop window with a counter and empty stools behind it, no words

panels.name: Open

panels.composition: Tier 3: the street from its end, the seawall, the bay, the ridge, the glow — the only thing on the page that hasn't changed. Held.

image.prompt: wet-on-wet watercolor in gray-green moss, fog and rusted tin, an empty small-town street seen from its end with a seawall and bay beyond and a warm glow above a distant ridge, no words

panels.name: Noon

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; the pup's weight learned; Sundays wet-on-wet

notes: Nobody. OPEN for no one. The glow unchanged.
